steps.title: Sancerre
steps.body: Sancerre, on the left bank of the upper Loire, makes 100% Sauvignon Blanc whites from hillside vineyards. Its style is crisp and restrained, with citrus, gooseberry, white flowers and a mineral, flinty edge. Sancerre also makes red and rosé from Pinot Noir. Nearby Menetou-Salon, Quincy and Reuilly make similar wines.

steps.title: Soils
steps.body: Three soils shape Sancerre: terres blanches, Kimmeridgian clay-limestone, giving full, structured wines; caillottes, stony limestone, giving fresh, aromatic wines; and silex, flint, giving smoky, mineral, long-lived wines. Pouilly-Fumé, across the river, is known for its flint and a smoky, gunflint character, hence fumé, smoky.

steps.prompt: Match each soil to its Sancerre style.

steps.body: Didier Dagueneau, in Pouilly-Fumé, made some of the world's most celebrated Sauvignon Blanc, showing how long it can age from great sites.

steps.prompt: What does fumé in Pouilly-Fumé refer to?
steps.explanation: Fumé means smoky, linked to its flint soils and the grape's bloom.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Sancerre is crisp, restrained and mineral
Terres blanches, caillottes and silex give different styles
Pouilly-Fumé is known for smoky, flinty wines
